steps.body: A number line gives every number a home: bigger numbers live to the right, and each mark's position IS its value.
steps.narration: A number line gives every number a home: bigger numbers live to the right, and each mark's position IS its value.

widget.prompt: Start at the mark labeled 40 and take one ten-hop to visit 50.

commonLandings.feedback: That single step visits 41 — the neighbor one ONE away, not one TEN.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10, going forward. From 40, 1 hops land on 50.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 50 — one ten to the right of 40, exactly where its size puts it.

options.label: To the right — it is bigger

predict.reveal: Bigger numbers always sit farther right; 67 outranks 50, so it lives rightward.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2l locate.
invariants: Position on the line IS the number: equal jumps cover equal amounts, and a journey's landing depends only on start, jump size, and direction for g2l locate.
misconceptions: Treating marks as decoration — unequal spacing, jumps of the wrong size, or reading a start mark as a landing.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which change — start, jump size, or direction — would move the landing, and which would leave it alone?

widget.prompt: A line shows marks at 40, 50, 60, 70. Where does 70 sit?

options.label: Exactly on the mark labeled 70
options.feedback: Correct — 70 is one of the labeled tens, so it sits right on its own mark.

options.label: Between 70 and 80
options.feedback: Between-the-marks is for numbers the labels skip; 70 IS a label here.

options.label: To the left of 40
options.feedback: 70 is larger than 40, and larger numbers live to the RIGHT on a number line.

options.label: Anywhere — position is a choice
options.feedback: A number line fixes every number's home by its size; position is never up for grabs.

steps.body: Locate a labeled mark by moving backward; the direction changes but every mark keeps one fixed value.

widget.prompt: Start at the mark labeled 70 and take one ten-hop backward to visit 60.

commonLandings.feedback: That is one unit left of 70. This line's labeled gaps are tens, so one hop reaches 60.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10 and this route goes backward. From 70, one hop lands on 60.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 60 — one ten to the left of 70. The labels anchor both position and direction.

widget.prompt: 50 + 5 = ? (the next mark when marks sit every 5)

commonErrors.feedback: That moved one — equally spaced marks here step by 5 every time.
That is a ten-step; this line's marks sit 5 apart.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Walk the line: find the start mark, take the jumps one at a time, and read the mark you land on.

widget.prompt: A line is labeled 20, 30, 40, 50. Where would 35 sit?

options.label: Halfway between the 30 and 40 marks
options.feedback: Correct — 35 is five after 30 and five before 40, so it sits halfway across that gap.

options.label: Directly on the 30 mark
options.feedback: 30 has its own labeled mark. The number 35 is five units farther to the right.

options.label: Directly on the 40 mark
options.feedback: 40 has its own labeled mark. The number 35 is five units before it.

options.label: To the left of the 20 mark
options.feedback: 35 is larger than 20, so its position must be to the right of 20 on the line.
